products.name: Activepieces
products.description: Open-source, AI-first workflow automation platform with 700+ integrations and MCP (Model Context Protocol) support enabling AI agents to build flows via natural language. Cloud and self-hosted deployment options.
products.positioning: AI-first automation for every team with modern UX and affordability
products.archetype: Visual workflow automation with AI copilot

products.name: Power Automate
products.description: Microsoft's enterprise workflow automation platform with cloud flows for integration and desktop flows (RPA) for UI automation. Deep integration with Microsoft 365, Dataverse, and Azure services. Gartner Leader in enterprise low-code platforms.
products.positioning: Enterprise workflow and RPA automation with Microsoft ecosystem lock-in
products.archetype: Enterprise cloud + RPA automation with Dataverse binding

products.name: Node-RED
products.description: Open-source, flow-based programming platform for event-driven applications. Originally from IBM, now under OpenJS Foundation governance. Focuses on industrial IoT, data processing, and enterprise workflows with 5000+ pre-built flows in community library.
products.positioning: Flow-based programming for event-driven and IoT applications with open-source flexibility
products.archetype: Flow-based visual programming with Node.js extensibility

products.name: Prismatic
products.description: Embedded iPaaS platform designed for B2B SaaS companies to embed workflow automation in their products. White-label embedded workflow builder with 70% development time savings claim. Enterprise-grade with Fortune 500 customers. Series B funded ($22M).
products.positioning: Embedded integration automation for B2B SaaS with white-label builder and enterprise scale
products.archetype: Embedded iPaaS workflow builder for product integration

products.name: Windmill
products.description: Code-first orchestration platform supporting Python, TypeScript, Go, Bash, and SQL. Designed for internal tools and workflows. Claims 13x faster execution vs Airflow. Open-source AGPLv3 with cloud and self-hosted options. YC S22 alum.
products.positioning: Code-first workflow orchestration optimized for developer experience and execution speed

products.name: Latenode
products.description: AI-native workflow automation platform with 1200+ app integrations and built-in LLM support. Unique CPU-second billing model offers 5x cost savings vs Make/Zapier. Bootstrapped with $2.1M ARR. High user satisfaction (4.9/5 Capterra).
products.positioning: Cost-efficient AI-native automation with built-in LLMs and pay-per-execution pricing
products.archetype: AI-first visual automation with novel cost model

products.name: n8n
products.description: Fair-code workflow automation with 400+ integrations and hybrid visual+code approach. Community edition free/self-hosted, enterprise licensed. Series C $180M, $2.5B valuation, $40M+ ARR. Extensive RAG workflow ecosystem (672+ templates). Leader in open-source automation.
products.positioning: Fair-code hybrid visual+code automation with enterprise backing and extensive integration library
products.archetype: Fair-code visual+code automation with extensive node library

notes:
Extraction covers 6 core products + n8n as market context reference (not in scope but critical for competitive positioning). Key findings:

1. **Market positioning**: Two dominant classes: (a) App-automation platforms (Activepieces, n8n, Latenode, Make, Zapier) focused on SaaS integrations; (b) Code-first tools (Windmill, Node-RED) for developers. Power Automate spans both via RPA.

2. **Threat level rationale**: High-threat products (Activepieces, Latenode, n8n, Power Automate) have 700-1200+ integrations, strong funding, and enterprise traction. MetroGraph's wedge = database-first schema visualization, which none emphasize. They chase feature/integration parity; MetroGraph has orthogonal UX advantage.

3. **MetroGraph's defensibility**: Schema introspection (ERD, relationship explorer, visual query building) is unique across this cohort. No competitor visualizes database structure natively. This is the moat.

4. **Feature scoring methodology**: Scored on (a) presence/support_level; (b) quality_grade (A=production-ready, mature; F=missing/broken); (c) hci_cost using pane counts and click depth from sources (e.g., Activepieces single-pane builder = A; Power Automate cloud flows also single-pane but more panels = B; Node-RED function node requires code = C for non-coders).

5. **Notable gaps in competitors**: 
   - No schema introspection across any (not their focus)
   - AI-assist features emerging but inconsistent (Latenode native, others via plugins)
   - Enterprise RBAC weak in open-source (Node-RED, Windmill) - only in Enterprise tiers
   - Onboarding templates strong (800-5000 flows) but mostly app-centric

6. **Sources coverage**: All products have T0 (official) and T1 (docs/API) coverage; T2 (analyst/review) for most; T3 (blog comparisons) for n8n, Activepieces, Windmill. Power Automate, Prismatic, Latenode have strong T1 and T2. Node-RED has community-driven T2/T3 but weaker official messaging.
